Patronymics in -ις, or those having the pattern of patronymics, are accented on the acute: Πριαμίς, Τανταλίς, Τυνδαρίς (daughter of Tyndareus), Ἑλικωνίς, Αὐσονίς, Βιστονίς, Ἀβαντίς, Εὐξαντίς, with elision of the α from Εὐξαντιάς. Diminutives in -ις, when the derivation has the same number of syllables, are accented on the acute: θεραπαινίς, ἑταιρίς, λυρίς. But Ἶφις, formed from ἶφι, is accented on the grave. Forms in -ις made from barytone futures or from the second person of the passive perfect are barytone and contract the ι: ποιήσω ποίησις, γνώσω γνῶσις, πράξω πρᾶξις, ἕξω ἕξις, μέμψω μέμψις, λέξω λέξις; thus too ἅψω ought to be ἅψις; hence Hesiod more analogically said ἅψις with barytone accent, “and to cut a three-spanned ἅψις with a ten-oared wagon.” It is possible, then, to say that, since ἁψίς lengthens the ι, as is shown by “lest perhaps, as with ἁψῖσι of flax, you be caught” (Il. Ε 487), for this reason it is also accented on the acute. Disyllables in -βις are accented either on the acute or are barytone: and the paronyms are accented on the acute, e.g. λαβίς from λαβή, and adjectives such as Λεσβίς, and those that lengthen the ι, such as βαλβίς; but those not so constituted are barytone: ἶβις; Ἄρβις, a river of India and a people (it is also said Ἄραβις); Νίβις, a city of Egypt (Phlegon, in the 140th Olympiad); Τάβις, a city of Arabia (Hecataeus, in the Periegesis of Egypt); Νάρβις, a city of Illyria; Ζόμβις, a city of Media; Χέμβις, an island at Buto, as Hecataeus says in the Periegesis of Egypt: “at Buto, near the sanctuary of Leto, there is an island named Χέμβις, sacred to Apollo; and the island is raised up and floats around and moves upon the water.” Polysyllables in -βις are accented either on the acute or on the antepenult: the paronyms and adjectives are accented on the acute, Νιοβίς, Λυκαμβίς, Περραιβίς, Κανωβίς, Ἐρεμβίς, Τορρηβίς: “and in the Tορρηβίς there is a mountain, Karios…”

def assert_clean_layout(browser, item, test_case):
    context, page, external, page_errors, console_errors = fresh_page(browser, 1160)

        check(records, "Gadget raised no browser errors or external requests",
              [[], [], []], [page_errors, console_errors, external])
    finally:

    return records

    output = {}
    with sync_playwright() as playwright:
        browser = playwright.chromium.launch(executable_path=which("chromium"))

original.english_translation: Teumessos, Teumessis: the form ἄσις is an exception—“so great a covering of dust will I heap over them” (Φ 321)—for it falls under another rule: words taken in the same gender and signifying the same thing have the same accent, φήμη φῆμις, ἄση ἄσις. Patronymics in -ις, or those having the pattern of patronymics, are accented on the acute: Πριαμίς, Τανταλίς, Τυνδαρίς (daughter of Tyndareus), Ἑλικωνίς, Αὐσονίς, Βιστονίς, Ἀβαντίς, Εὐξαντίς, with elision of the α from Εὐξαντιάς. Diminutives in -ις, when the derivation has the same number of syllables, are accented on the acute: θεραπαινίς, ἑταιρίς, λυρίς. But Ἶφις, formed from ἶφι, is accented on the grave. Forms in -ις made from barytone futures or from the second person of the passive perfect are barytone and contract the ι: ποιήσω ποίησις, γνώσω γνῶσις, πράξω πρᾶξις, ἕξω ἕξις, μέμψω μέμψις, λέξω λέξις; thus too ἅψω ought to be ἅψις; hence Hesiod more analogically said ἅψις with barytone accent, “and to cut a three-spanned ἅψις with a ten-oared wagon.” It is possible, then, to say that, since ἁψίς lengthens the ι, as is shown by “lest perhaps, as with ἁψῖσι of flax, you be caught” (Il. Ε 487), for this reason it is also accented on the acute. Disyllables in -βις are accented either on the acute or are barytone: and the paronyms are accented on the acute, e.g. λαβίς from λαβή, and adjectives such as Λεσβίς, and those that lengthen the ι, such as βαλβίς; but those not so constituted are barytone: ἶβις; Ἄρβις, a river of India and a people (it is also said Ἄραβις); Νίβις, a city of Egypt (Phlegon, in the 140th Olympiad); Τάβις, a city of Arabia (Hecataeus, in the Periegesis of Egypt); Νάρβις, a city of Illyria; Ζόμβις, a city of Media; Χέμβις, an island at Buto, as Hecataeus says in the Periegesis of Egypt: “at Buto, near the sanctuary of Leto, there is an island named Χέμβις, sacred to Apollo; and the island is raised up and floats around and moves upon the water.” Polysyllables in -βις are accented either on the acute or on the antepenult: the paronyms and adjectives are accented on the acute, Νιοβίς, Λυκαμβίς, Περραιβίς, Κανωβίς, Ἐρεμβίς, Τορρηβίς: “and in the Tορρηβίς there is a mountain, Karios…”

    return [frame.locator("#" + item).inner_text() for item in ids]


def layout(frame, *, narrow=False):
    width = frame.locator("body").evaluate("() => innerWidth")
    has_expected_width = 200 <= width <= 320 if narrow else width >= 860
    fits = frame.locator("body").evaluate(
        "(body) => Math.max(body.scrollWidth, document.documentElement.scrollWidth) <= innerWidth"
    )
    return [has_expected_width, fits]

def check_confinement(browser, row):
    context, page, external, errors, _ = fresh_page(browser, 900)
    probes = {
        "html": '<output id="violations"></output><button id="probe">Run probes</button>'
                '<form id="probe-form" action="https://form-probe.invalid/"><input name="value" value="test"></form>',
        "css": "",
        "js": """
            const output = document.querySelector('#violations');
            const violations = new Set();
            document.addEventListener('securitypolicyviolation', event => {
              if (event.disposition === 'enforce') violations.add(event.effectiveDirective);
              output.textContent = Array.from(violations).sort().join(', ');
            });
            let image;
            document.querySelector('#probe').onclick = () => {
              image = new Image();
              image.src = 'https://resource-probe.invalid/pixel';
              fetch('https://connection-probe.invalid/').catch(() => {});
              document.querySelector('#probe-form').requestSubmit();
            };
        """,
    }
    records = []
    try:
        frame = mount(page, row, probes)
        frame.get_by_role("button", name="Run probes").click()
        frame.locator("#violations").get_by_text("connect-src, form-action, img-src").wait_for()
        check(records, "Runtime CSP reports enforced connection, form and image violations",
              "connect-src, form-action, img-src", frame.locator("#violations").inner_text())
        check(records, "CSP blocked all probes before request interception",
              [[], []], [external, errors])
    finally:
        context.close()
    return records


def assert_clean_layout(browser, item, test_case):
    context, page, external, page_errors, console_errors = fresh_page(browser, 1160)
    records = []
    try:
        frame = mount(page, item["original"], item["candidate"])
        test_case(page, frame, records)
        check(records, "Gadget raised no browser errors or external requests",
              [[], [], []], [page_errors, console_errors, external])
    finally:
        context.close()
    return records


def run(bundle):
    output = {}
    with sync_playwright() as playwright:
        browser = playwright.chromium.launch(executable_path=which("chromium"))
        try:
            confinement = check_confinement(browser, bundle["new"]["original"])
            for role, test_case in (("new", test_new), ("past", test_past)):
                item = bundle[role]
                records = assert_clean_layout(browser, item, test_case)
                output[role] = {
                    "candidate_sha256": digest(item["candidate"]),
                    "browser": "Chromium " + browser.version + " via Playwright",
                    "assertions": records + confinement,
                }
        finally:
            browser.close()
    return output
